titolo: How Did Roman Soldiers Survive Freezing Nights Without Heaters? The Brutal 400-Year Secret

scene.testo: It is February on the northern frontier. The wind is coming off the moors at 40 miles an hour. The temperature is below freezing, and a Roman soldier stands on a stone wall in the dark.

He has no heater, no thermal jacket, no sleeping bag, and no way to leave his post. He will stand there for 3 hours. Then he will sleep in a stone room with no glass in the window, and in the morning he will get up and do his job.
Here is the part that should not make sense. Men like him did this for 400 years. Not one bad winter, four centuries, across Britain, the Rhine, the Danube, and the mountains of Armenia.
They had no chimneys the way we think of chimneys. They had no cotton. They had no down. They had no matches.

And yet the Roman army lost fewer men to cold than almost any army that came after it for the next thousand years. Napoleon's army froze in Russia. So how did the Romans pull it off? What was their secret?

descrizione:
How did Roman soldiers survive freezing nights without heaters? Picture a legionary on Hadrian's Wall in February, wind at 40 miles an hour, below freezing, no thermal jacket and no sleeping bag, standing watch for 3 hours.

For 400 years, Roman soldiers endured brutal winters across Britain, the Rhine, the Danube and the mountains of Armenia. No cotton, no down, no matches, no modern chimneys.

Yet the Roman army lost fewer men to cold than almost any army for the next thousand years, while Napoleon's army froze in Russia. What was the secret of Roman winter survival? Watch to find out.
